## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system exhibits a critical operational deficiency. While routine maintenance was performed and most components remain in good condition, the effluent pump is running without hydraulic load. This indicates a severe mechanical or plumbing failure that requires immediate professional attention.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches and represents 22.9 percent of the total fluid depth. This is within the normal range and does not yet indicate a need for pumping.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | Baffles intact; no visible damage |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated; light soiling |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 HP, 115V) | CRITICAL | See Pump Performance section below |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no breakout observed |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |

## PUMP PERFORMANCE
**CRITICAL FINDING:**

The effluent pump measured 1.6 amps during operation against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This represents 22.2 percent of full-load amperage. The pump is running but drawing no hydraulic load.

This condition indicates one or more of the following:
- The impeller is broken or missing
- The discharge line is severed or disconnected
- The pump is running dry (no fluid present at the inlet)

A pump operating without load will overheat rapidly and sustain motor damage. The system cannot treat or disperse effluent while the pump is non-functional.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**Immediate Action Required:**

1. **Pump Failure -- CRITICAL.** The effluent pump is operating without hydraulic load. Immediate professional attention is required to diagnose and repair the pump, impeller, or discharge line. Do not delay this repair. Continued operation risks motor failure and complete loss of system function.

**Routine Maintenance:**

2. The effluent filter was cleaned during this visit and showed only light soiling. Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval.

3. Solids content is within normal range. No pumping is required at this time. Continue monitoring at routine maintenance visits.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Immediate Concern: Pump Failure

Your system's effluent pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious problem that will prevent your system from treating and dispersing wastewater. The pump motor is at risk of overheating and burning out if operation continues.

Contact a septic service professional immediately to inspect the pump, check the discharge line for breaks or disconnections, and confirm that water is reaching the pump inlet. Do not attempt to operate the system beyond normal household use while this issue is unresolved.

### Solids Management

Your tank solids are at a healthy level (about 23 percent of tank volume). The scum and sludge layers are accumulating at a normal rate. To keep solids from building up faster than expected, avoid flushing non-biodegradable items -- wipes, paper towels, feminine hygiene products, dental floss, cooking grease, and medications. These materials do not break down in the tank and will shorten the time until pumping becomes necessary.
